newsitem.title: NORWAY: It's do or die for Norway's Fokus Bank.
newsitem.headline: It's do or die for Norway's Fokus Bank.

text.p: Norway's Fokus Bank is fighting two battles -- one it can afford to lose and another that would spell its demise from the country's crowded financial sector, analysts said on Wednesday.
They said Fokus could live with a defeat in the month-long battle with Den norske Bank (DnB) for mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken (BNbank).
But Fokus this week was confronted with a hostile takeover bid from Sparebankgruppen, a group of sixteen regional savings banks out to swallow the country's fourth largest bank.
Analysts speculated a foreign bidder, possibly a Swedish or Danish bank, might rescue Fokus from Sparebankgruppen, which now controls 10 percent of the bank.
Fokus is 80 percent owned by foreign investors.

"Fokus is looking for other bidders now," said an Oslo-based financial analyst. "To be bought by Sparebankengruppen would be the worst thing that could happen to Fokus because they would carve it up. Everything else would be a blessing."

Fokus, which specialises in regional banking, announced on Tuesday that its first-quarter after-tax profits jumped by 56.5 percent to 182.5 million crowns ($26.1 million) compared with the same 1996 period.
It moved forward the date for its result announcement by ten days following Sparebankgruppen's bid on Monday.
But analysts said the result was not significant enough to increase the price of the bank, which was valued at 4.80 billion crowns by Sparebankgruppen.
The group said a takeover was conditional on Fokus not acquiring BNbank.

But the chances of Fokus winning that battle were further reduced on Wednesday when DnB, the country's biggest bank, raised its cash offer for BNbank to 209 crowns per share from 207 crowns, including dividend.

The DnB's new bid valued BNbank at 2.04 billion crowns, compared with Fokus' share exchange offer pricing BNbank at 2.06 billion crowns. The mortgage lender last week inclined towards accepting DnB's bid but no decision has yet been made.
"I think DnB wins BNbank and that there will be a rival bid for Fokus that is higher than Sparebankegruppen's. The rival bid will come from abroad," another Oslo-based analyst said.
Fokus has been the most heavily traded share on the Oslo Bourse for three consecutive sessions but DnB and other major Norwegian banks have denied involvement.
Sweden's Handelsbanken, which has been tipped as a possible suitor, has refused comment while Denmark's Den Danske Bank (DDB) has said it has no plans to buy a Norwegian bank.
"I think Handelsbanken or Den Danske Bank will bid for Fokus, regardless of what Den Danske Bank is saying," the analyst said.

Another analyst doubted Handelsbanken would try to buy Fokus, noting it had just recently finalised the acquisition of mortgage lender Stadshypotek. "Handelsbanken would have to make a share issue to get the necessary capital. They want to digest Stadshypotek now."
Fokus was being traded at 73.50 crowns on Wednesday at 1400 gmt, 0.50 crowns above the Sparebanken bid.
Nils Ringdal, a Dresdner Kleinwort Benson analyst, said the market was clearly looking for a second bid.

"But, honestly, I am not sure there will be one. I believe a share price of 73 crowns is a very high price for Fokus if you take current profitablity into account. You cannot defend that price unless you have a substantial amount of synergy or you are willing to pay that price to enter the market."
He said consolidation in the sector was far from over.
"If you can remove a competitor from the market, which is what Sparebankgruppen is trying to do, you will ease pressure on the margins," Ringdal said. ($ = 6.999 Norwegian Crowns)
